Topics.Title: Managing a Course as a Git Repository in PreseMaker
Topics.Summary: Covers how PreseMaker enables version control for courses without command-line git, including initializing a repository, committing changes, pushing to a remote, and pulling updates through PreseMaker's built-in interface.

Elements.Title: Initializing a Git Repository for a Course
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker allows you to place any course under version control by initializing a git repository directly from within the application.
Elements.Notes: This eliminates the need to open a terminal or run any command-line instructions. Once initialized, the course folder is tracked as a git repository managed entirely through PreseMaker.

Items.Text: The initialize action sets up git tracking for the course from inside PreseMaker's interface, requiring no command-line interaction.
Once a repository is initialized, PreseMaker stores the associated git settings, such as the remote URL and target branch, for that course.
This is a one-time setup step performed before committing or pushing changes for the first time.

Elements.Title: Committing Changes with a Message
Elements.BodyText: After making edits to a course, you can record a snapshot of those changes by creating a commit through PreseMaker's built-in interface.
Elements.Notes: Committing regularly with descriptive messages helps you track the history of changes and makes it easier to identify what was updated at each stage of course development.

Items.Text: A commit captures the current state of the course and requires you to provide a commit message describing what changed.
PreseMaker performs the underlying git commit operation on your behalf, so no terminal commands are needed.
Committing does not automatically send changes to a remote; that is a separate push action.

Elements.Title: Pushing Changes to a Remote Repository
Elements.BodyText: Once changes are committed locally, PreseMaker enables you to push those commits to a configured remote repository such as one hosted on GitHub.
Elements.Notes: PreseMaker remembers the last time a push was performed for each course, giving you a reference point for how up to date the remote copy is.

Items.Text: Pushing sends your local commits to the remote repository, making the latest version of the course available outside your local machine.
The remote URL is stored in PreseMaker's course git settings and does not need to be re-entered each time you push.
PreseMaker records the timestamp of the last successful push so you can easily see whether your remote is current.

Elements.Title: Pulling Updates from a Remote Repository
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker also supports pulling changes from a remote repository, allowing you to bring in updates that exist on the remote but not yet on your local copy.
Elements.Notes: This is useful when collaborating or when you have made changes on another machine and need to sync your current working environment.

Items.Text: The pull action retrieves and integrates changes from the configured remote repository into your local course.
PreseMaker performs this operation through its interface, removing the need to run git pull in a terminal.
You can also check for incoming changes before pulling to be aware of what updates are available from the remote.

Elements.Title: Checking for Incoming Changes and Conflicts
Elements.BodyText: Before pulling, PreseMaker allows you to check whether there are incoming changes on the remote that differ from your local version.
Elements.Notes: Being aware of incoming changes before pulling helps you make an informed decision about when to sync. Note that manual merge-conflict resolution and branch management are outside PreseMaker's built-in workflow.

Items.Text: PreseMaker can compare your local state against the remote to surface whether any updates are waiting to be pulled.
This check helps you avoid unexpected overwrites by making you aware of differences before you commit to pulling.
Advanced git operations such as branch management and pull requests are not part of PreseMaker's interface and fall outside this workflow.

Elements.Title: Stored Git Settings per Course
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker maintains a set of git configuration details for each course, so you do not need to reconfigure version control every time you work on a project.
Elements.Notes: Having settings stored per course means PreseMaker can handle repeated push and pull operations seamlessly without prompting you to re-enter configuration details each session.

Items.Text: Each course stores its own remote URL, branch, and last-pushed timestamp within PreseMaker.
These stored settings allow PreseMaker to perform git operations consistently without requiring manual input on each action.
Updating these settings can be done from within the PreseMaker interface if the remote location or other details change.

Topics.Title: Publishing a Course Website with GitHub Pages
Topics.Summary: Explains how PreseMaker connects a course to GitHub and publishes the exported website through GitHub Pages, giving the course a live public web address without manual configuration on GitHub.

Elements.Title: Exporting the Course Website Before Publishing
Elements.BodyText: Before PreseMaker can publish a course online, you first export it as a website from within the application.
Elements.Notes: The export step produces the static web files that GitHub Pages will serve. This is a prerequisite to the publishing step.

Items.Text: PreseMaker includes a built-in export function that packages your course as a complete website ready for hosting.
The exported files are what GitHub Pages will deliver to learners when they visit the course's public web address.
You initiate this export from inside PreseMaker — no external tools or manual file management are required at this stage.

Elements.Title: Connecting the Course to a GitHub Repository
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker handles the connection between your course and a GitHub repository directly through its own interface, without requiring you to configure anything manually on the GitHub website.
Elements.Notes: PreseMaker stores each course's git settings, including the remote URL, so the connection only needs to be established once per course.

Items.Text: You provide the remote repository URL inside PreseMaker, and it stores that setting for the course going forward.
PreseMaker remembers the repository association and last-push status, so you do not need to re-enter connection details each session.
PreseMaker guides the GitHub connection and publishing so you do not have to configure git or GitHub Pages by hand; you do need a GitHub account and a repository to publish to.

Elements.Title: Publishing Through PreseMaker Rather Than GitHub's Website
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker assists with the full GitHub Pages publishing process so that you never need to navigate GitHub's settings pages or run git commands manually.
Elements.Notes: This design keeps the entire publishing workflow inside one application, lowering the technical barrier for course authors.

Items.Text: All publishing actions — including pushing the exported website files to the repository — are triggered from within PreseMaker's interface.
PreseMaker performs the underlying git push operation on your behalf, so no command-line interaction is required.
Because PreseMaker handles the GitHub Pages setup, authors can publish without prior experience configuring hosting settings on GitHub.

Elements.Title: The Live Public Web Address
Elements.BodyText: Once published, the course receives a live public web address through GitHub Pages, making it accessible to learners anywhere with a browser.
Elements.Notes: GitHub Pages generates a URL automatically based on the repository; PreseMaker surfaces this address so you can share it with learners.

Items.Text: GitHub Pages assigns a public URL to the repository, turning the exported course files into a fully hosted website.
Learners can visit the course at that web address without needing any special access or account.
The address remains stable as long as the repository and its Pages configuration remain active, giving you a reliable link to share.

Elements.Title: Pushing Updates to the Published Site
Elements.BodyText: When you revise a course and re-export it, PreseMaker lets you push the updated files to the same repository, refreshing the live website.
Elements.Notes: PreseMaker tracks when the course was last pushed, helping you identify whether the live site reflects your most recent edits.

Items.Text: After making changes and re-exporting, you use PreseMaker's push action to send the updated website files to the GitHub repository.
GitHub Pages automatically serves the latest pushed files, so the public URL reflects your updates shortly after the push completes.
PreseMaker's record of the last push time helps you confirm that the live site is in sync with your current course content.

Topics.Title: Using the Course Repository Service
Topics.Summary: Describes PreseMaker's integration with external course-repository services, covering how to import course materials from a shared repository and publish your own materials for others to access and reuse.

Elements.Title: What the Course Repository Service Is
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker integrates with an external course-repository service — such as floridacourserepo.com — that functions as a content-sharing hub for educators.
Elements.Notes: This service is entirely separate from git version control. It is focused on discovering and distributing ready-made course materials, not on tracking code changes or managing branches.

Items.Text: The course repository service is a dedicated platform for sharing and reusing course content across institutions or instructors.
It is accessed from within PreseMaker, so you do not need to visit or configure the external site manually.
The service is not a git workflow — no commands, personal access tokens, or branch management are involved.

Elements.Title: Connecting to the Repository Service from PreseMaker
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker provides a built-in interface to connect to the course-repository service, keeping the process inside the application.
Elements.Notes: Because the connection is handled by PreseMaker's interface, instructors are not required to set up accounts or API credentials outside of what PreseMaker guides them through.

Items.Text: The connection to the external repository service is initiated and managed from within PreseMaker's own interface.
PreseMaker stores the relevant service settings so you do not need to re-enter connection details each session.
PreseMaker handles the connection to the course-repository service from within the app once you provide the repository details it needs.

Elements.Title: Importing Course Materials from the Repository
Elements.BodyText: Through the course-repository service, you can browse and import course materials that others have published, bringing them directly into PreseMaker for use or adaptation.
Elements.Notes: Importing from the repository is a way to avoid building courses from scratch — you can start with an existing published course and customize it to fit your needs.

Items.Text: PreseMaker allows you to search or browse the shared repository for course materials created by other educators.
Selected materials are imported into PreseMaker, where you can use them as-is or modify them for your own course.
The import process is handled through PreseMaker's interface rather than by manually downloading and re-uploading files.

Elements.Title: Publishing Your Materials to the Repository
Elements.BodyText: You can contribute your own course materials to the shared repository through PreseMaker, making them available for other educators to discover and reuse.
Elements.Notes: Publishing to the course repository is a separate action from pushing to a git remote or deploying to GitHub Pages — it is specifically about sharing content with the broader educator community through the repository service.

Items.Text: PreseMaker provides an option to publish a course to the external repository service directly from within the application.
Once published, your materials become accessible to other users of the same repository service, such as floridacourserepo.com.
Publishing is focused on content sharing and reuse, not on version tracking or web deployment.

Elements.Title: How the Repository Service Differs from Other PreseMaker Features
Elements.BodyText: The course-repository service fills a distinct role compared to PreseMaker's git integration and GitHub Pages publishing, and it is important to understand where each feature applies.
Elements.Notes: Keeping these three features — git version control, GitHub Pages publishing, and the course repository service — clearly separated helps you choose the right tool for each goal.

Items.Text: Git version control in PreseMaker is for tracking changes to your course over time; the repository service is for sharing finished or in-progress content with others.
GitHub Pages publishing gives your course a public web address; the repository service makes your course materials available for other instructors to import and reuse.
The course repository service is a content-sharing network, not a deployment or version-history tool.

Topics.Title: Other Sharing Options: Archive Export and iFrame Embedding
Topics.Summary: Introduces additional ways to share course content, including exporting a course as a portable archive file for import elsewhere and generating an iFrame embed code to display course content within another web page.

Elements.Title: Overview of Additional Sharing Options
Elements.BodyText: Beyond version control and GitHub Pages, PreseMaker provides two supplementary methods for distributing course content to different audiences and platforms.
Elements.Notes: These options are especially useful when learners or collaborators do not have direct access to a GitHub Pages URL or a course repository service.

Items.Text: Archive export allows a course to be packaged into a single portable file that can be moved and imported elsewhere.
iFrame embedding allows course content to be displayed inside another web page without requiring the viewer to navigate away.
Both options complement the primary sharing workflows and can be used independently or alongside them.

Elements.Title: Exporting a Course as an Archive File
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker can export an entire course as a self-contained archive file, making the course portable and importable into another environment.
Elements.Notes: This is useful for sharing courses offline, transferring content between accounts, or creating a backup snapshot of a course at a specific point in time.

Items.Text: The export process packages all course materials into a single archive file from within the PreseMaker interface.
The resulting archive file can be imported into PreseMaker elsewhere, allowing the course to be reused or edited in a different context.
Archive export does not require a network connection or a linked repository, making it a fully offline sharing method.

Elements.Title: When to Use Archive Export
Elements.BodyText: Archive export is best suited for situations where a portable, standalone copy of the course is needed rather than a live published link.
Elements.Notes: Consider archive export when distributing to collaborators who need to edit the course locally, when internet access is limited, or when migrating content between platforms.

Items.Text: Use archive export to hand off a complete course to another instructor or institution for local use.
Archive files serve as point-in-time snapshots, providing a form of manual backup separate from version control history.
Importing an archive restores the course content so it can be continued or modified in PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Generating an iFrame Embed Code
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker can generate an iFrame embed code that allows course content to be displayed directly within another web page.
Elements.Notes: An iFrame (inline frame) is a standard HTML element that loads an external web page inside a designated area of a host page, so viewers see the course content without leaving the host site.

Items.Text: PreseMaker produces the embed code automatically, so no manual HTML authoring is required.
The generated code can be pasted into the HTML of any web page that supports iFrame embedding, such as a course portal or institutional website.
The embedded content reflects the published version of the course, meaning updates to the published course are reflected in the embedded view.

Elements.Title: When to Use iFrame Embedding
Elements.BodyText: iFrame embedding is the preferred option when course content needs to appear seamlessly within an existing website or learning management system page.
Elements.Notes: This approach keeps learners on a familiar host page while still delivering the full PreseMaker course experience within that page's layout.

Items.Text: Use iFrame embedding when an institution or instructor wants to present course content inside a branded portal without redirecting learners to an external URL.
iFrame embedding requires that the course already be published to a publicly accessible web address, such as a GitHub Pages URL.
The host page controls the dimensions and placement of the embedded frame, allowing the course to be sized and positioned to fit the surrounding design.

Elements.Title: Comparing Archive Export and iFrame Embedding
Elements.BodyText: Although both options extend how course content is shared, they serve distinct purposes and suit different distribution scenarios.
Elements.Notes: Choosing the right option depends on whether the goal is to transfer editable content (archive) or to display published content in another context (iFrame).

Items.Text: Archive export produces an editable, importable file, while iFrame embedding displays a live published course inside another page.
Archive export works without a published web address; iFrame embedding requires one.
Use archive export for content transfer or backup, and use iFrame embedding for integrated, in-page presentation to learners.

Topics.Title: Choosing the Right Sharing Method
Topics.Summary: Helps learners compare all available sharing and distribution options — version control, GitHub Pages, course repository, archive export, and iFrame — so they can identify which best fits a given use case.

Elements.Title: Overview of Available Sharing Methods
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker offers several distinct ways to share and distribute course content, each serving a different purpose and audience.
Elements.Notes: Understanding the full landscape of options before choosing one prevents mismatches between the method and the intended outcome.

Items.Text: The five primary methods are: version control (git), GitHub Pages, the course repository service, archive export, and iFrame embedding.
Each method differs in how content is stored, who can access it, and what technical steps are involved.
Selecting the right method depends on factors such as collaboration needs, public visibility, reusability, and integration with other platforms.

Elements.Title: Version Control for Ongoing Course Development
Elements.BodyText: Using PreseMaker's built-in git integration is best suited for tracking changes over time and maintaining a reliable history of a course.
Elements.Notes: This method is ideal when a single author or small team needs to commit incremental updates, revert mistakes, or keep a remote backup — not for public content distribution on its own.

Items.Text: Choose version control when you need a change history, the ability to push and pull updates, or a remote backup of course files.
This method is managed entirely inside PreseMaker — no command-line git knowledge is required.
Version control alone does not make course content publicly accessible; it is a development and safety workflow, not a distribution channel.

Elements.Title: GitHub Pages for Public Web Publishing
Elements.BodyText: GitHub Pages takes an exported course website and gives it a live, public web address that anyone can visit in a browser.
Elements.Notes: This is the right choice when the goal is to deliver a course as a standalone website to learners who simply need a URL — no login or special software required.

Items.Text: Use GitHub Pages when you want to publish a course website publicly and share it via a direct link.
PreseMaker handles the connection to GitHub and the publishing process, so no manual configuration on the GitHub website is needed.
GitHub Pages works alongside version control — the repository stores the files, and GitHub Pages serves them as a website.

Elements.Title: The Course Repository Service for Content Sharing
Elements.BodyText: The course repository service (such as floridacourserepo.com) is a dedicated platform for discovering, importing, and publishing reusable course materials within a community.
Elements.Notes: This method is distinct from git — it is a content-sharing marketplace rather than a code-versioning tool, and it does not involve branches, pull requests, or personal access tokens.

Items.Text: Choose the course repository service when you want to share materials with a broader educator community or adopt materials others have already created.
You can both publish your own courses to the repository and import existing materials from it directly inside PreseMaker.
This option prioritizes reusability and community distribution, making it different from simply hosting a website or tracking file changes.

Elements.Title: Archive Export for Portable, Offline Distribution
Elements.BodyText: Exporting a course as an archive file packages all course content into a single transferable file that can be imported into another PreseMaker instance.
Elements.Notes: Archive export is the simplest method when internet connectivity, repository accounts, or public hosting are not available or necessary.

Items.Text: Use archive export when you need to hand off course files directly to another person or move a course to a different machine without using cloud services.
This method requires no internet connection, GitHub account, or third-party service.
The recipient must import the archive into PreseMaker, making it best suited for closed or controlled distribution rather than open public access.

Elements.Title: iFrame Embedding for Integration with Other Platforms
Elements.BodyText: An iFrame embed code lets you display course content inside an existing web page, learning management system, or other platform without redirecting learners to a separate site.
Elements.Notes: This is the preferred choice when course content must appear seamlessly within a larger website or LMS rather than as a standalone destination.

Items.Text: Choose iFrame embedding when learners should experience the course content within a host platform they are already using.
The embed code generated by PreseMaker can be pasted into any platform that supports HTML iFrames.
iFrame embedding typically requires that the course is already hosted somewhere accessible — such as via GitHub Pages — so it often pairs with another sharing method.

Elements.Title: Matching the Method to the Use Case
Elements.BodyText: Each sharing method has a specific sweet spot, and the best choice depends on the combination of your collaboration needs, audience, and technical environment.
Elements.Notes: In practice, methods can be combined — for example, using version control for development, GitHub Pages for hosting, and an iFrame to embed the result in an LMS.

Items.Text: If the priority is change tracking and safe development, use version control through PreseMaker's git integration.
If the priority is giving learners a public URL, publish via GitHub Pages; if it is community reuse among educators, use the course repository service.
If simplicity and portability matter most, export an archive; if seamless integration into an existing platform is needed, use an iFrame embed code.
